This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call
vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https ://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/Virtua!Meeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bsa1eaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/Virtua!Meeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency.
In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and
public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be
physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which
are not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although
no action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak
during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to
speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and
follow the directions for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are
not subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been
submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public
comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Subject:  Art in Public Places Ordinance

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report on the Art in Public Places
Ordinance and associated funds received by the City.

DISCUSSION: One of the Commission's Council-approved work assignments for Fiscal
Year 2022-2023 is to review and recommend policies, procedures, and projects in
accordance with the Art in Public Places Ordinance.

On September 8, 2014, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 382 for Art in Public
Places (Ordinance) , establishing a public art requirement for certain commercial,
institutional, and multi-family residential development projects (Attachment 1). _The
Ordinance was developed to enhance the quality of life for individuals living in, working in,
and visiting the City of Malibu through Cultural and artistic resources.

On August 14, 2017, the Council adopted Resolution 17-35 (Attachment 2) , establishing
implementation guidelines (Guidelines) for the Ordinance. The Ordinance and Guidelines
were crafted with feedback from the Cultural Arts Commission, the Zoning and Ordinance
Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee, and the Planning Commission .

On November 23, 2021 , the · Commission received and filed a report outlining the
requirements, criteria, and fund balance.

On March 28, 2023, the Commission requested the Arts in Public Places Ordinance to be
placed on the April 25, 2023 Regular Meeting agenda for discussion.

Under the Ordinance, property owners must meet specific public art requirements for
projects that fall within the following criteria:

  •  New commercial or institutional development, excluding city and public school
  projects, when the total construction cost exceeds $250,000.
  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item #4.B.
   •  Remodel or reconstruction of an existing commercial or institutional development,
  excluding city and public school projects, when the total construction cost exceeds
  $250,000.
  •  New multi-family residential development, with four or more units and abutting a
  public or private street, which is open to the public, when the total construction cost
  exceeds $250,000.
  •  Remodel or reconstruction of an existing multi-family residential development, with
  four or more units and abutting a public or private street, which is open to the public,
  when the total construction cost exceeds $250,000.

If the project meets any one of the criteria noted above, the property is owner is required
completed one of the following public art requirements:

  1. Acquire and install public art on the project site, or an alternative site within and
  acceptable to the city, consistent with the Guidelines equal to at least two percent
  of the project's total construction cost.
  2. Make a contribution to the City's Public Art Fund in-lieu of the placement of public
  art equal to at least one percent of the project's total construction cost.

If the property owner decides to acquire and install public art, the art work must follow the
requirements and process outlined in the Guidelines. The process includes details about
the selection criteria of the art work and requires approval from the City, Council, and
various Commissions, including the Malibu Arts Commission. If the property owner
decides to make a contribution in-lieu of acquiring and installing public art, the contribution
is deposited into the City's Public Art Fund. Currently, the Public Art Fund has a balance
of approximately $35,600.

Section 2.  Environmental Review.

The City Council has analyzed the project proposal described herein. The California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) applies only to projects which have the potential for causing a significant effect on
the environment. Pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), where it can be seen with certainty
that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment,
the activity is not subject to CEQA. The City Council determined that there is no possibility the
amendment will have a significant effect on the environment and accordingly, the exemption set forth in
Section 15061(b)(3) applies. Individual art projects will be subject to subsequent CEQA review.

Section 3.  Findings. Pursuant to M.M.C. Section 17.74.040, the City Council hereby fmds that this
amendment has been processed in accordance with state law and the Malibu Municipal Code (M.M.C.)
and that the amendment is consistent with the General Plan.

  A. The subject zoning text amendment is consistent with the objectives, policies, general
  land uses and programs specified in the General Plan. The proposed amendment serves to enhance
  the Malibu General Plan Mission Statement and preserve Malibu's natural and cultural resources.

  B. The Planning Commission held public hearings on the amendment and considered,
  deliberated and deadlocked over whether to recommend approval of the amendment.

17.59.010  Intent and Purpose.

Cultural and artistic resources enhance the quality of life for individuals living in, working in, and visiting
the City of Malibu. Visually pleasing, high-quality public art contributes to a unique sense of community

  ATTACHMENT 1
   Ordinance No. 382
  Page3 of6

and enriches the quality of life for residents and visitors alike. Therefore, the city council declares that it is
in the public interest to require the incorporation of public artwork into certain new or remodeled
commercial, institutional, and multi-family development projects.

17.59.020  Definitions.

Unless the context otherwise requires, the defmitions set forth in this section shall govern the construction
of this chapter. In addition, except as provided in this chapter, the definitions contained in Sections
17.02.050 and 17.02.060 shall also govern the construction of this chapter.

"Art" or "Artwork" means an original work of a permanent nature in any variety of media produced by an
artist and which may include sculptures, murals, photography and original works of graphic art, glass,
mosaics, or any combination or forms of media, furnishings or fixtures permanently affixed to the
building or its grounds, or a combination thereof. Artwork shall not include decorative, ornamental or
functional elements designed by the architect, or other design consultant retained for the design and
construction of the subject building, or pieces that are mass produced with a standard design such as
fountains and statuary objects.

"Art in Public Places Implementing Guidelines" means those procedures, guidelines, and requirements
adopted by the city council for the selection, approval, acquisition, and installation of public art.

"Public art" means art or artwork intended for placement or installation in a public place pursuant to the
Art in Public Places Implementing Guidelines.

"Public place" means the exterior area on a public or private property within the city, which is open,
easily accessible and clearly visible to the public.

"Total construction cost" means the total valuation of the proposed structure and improvements as
calculated by the building official utilizing the most current International Code Council cost estimator for
new construction, and actual contract bid price for remodels or reconstruction. Land costs and off-site
improvement costs are excluded.

"Value of art or artwork" means the cost of the public art, as determined pursuant to the Art in Public
Places Implementing Guidelines, which must be equal to at least two percent of the project's total
construction cost.

17.59.030  Applicability.

A.  The provisions of this chapter shall apply to the following qualifying development projects, unless
the exceptions or exemptions in subsections Band C of this section apply:

  1.  New commercial or institutional development, excluding city and public school projects,
when the total construction cost exceeds two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000).

  2.  Remodel or reconstruction of an existing commercial or institutional development,
excluding city and public school projects, when the total construction cost exceeds two hundred fifty
thousand dollars ($250,000).

  ATTACHMENT 1
   Ordinance No. 382
  Page4 of6

  3.  New multi-family residential development, with four or more units and abutting a public or
private street, which is open to the public, when the total construction cost exceeds two hundred fifty
thousand dollars ($250,000).

  4.  Remodel or reconstruction of an existing multi-family residential development, with four
or more units and abutting a public or private street, which is open to the public, when the total
construction cost exceeds two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000).

B.  Exceptions. The requirements of this chapter shall not apply to the following activities:

  1.  Repair or maintenance activities that do not result in an addition to, or enlargement of the
structure or structures being repaired or maintained.

  2.  The reconstruction of any structure destroyed by natural disaster provided the replacement
structure complies with all of the following:

  a.  It is for the same use and occupancy as the destroyed structure;

  b.  It does not exceed the floor area, height, or volume of the destroyed structure by
more than ten percent; and

  c.  It is sited in the same location on the property as the destroyed structure.

  3.  The remodel or reconstruction of any development that has already provided public art in
accordance with this chapter.

C.  Exemptions. The following categories of projects shall not be subject to this chapter.

  1.  Projects having a fully executed development agreement or a vesting tentative map
approved prior to the effective date of this chapter.

  2.  Projects for which a building permit was issued prior to the effective date of this chapter.

17.59.040  Requirement to Provide Public Art or Pay In-Lieu Contribution.

When a project is subject to the requirements of this chapter, the property owner shall comply with either
subsections A or B of this section prior to final inspection by the City of Malibu Environmental
Sustainability Department or issuance of certificate of occupancy. The obligations of subsections A and
B of this section shall be binding on the property owner's heirs, successors and assigns.

A.  The property owner shall acquire and install public art on the project site, or an alternative site
within and acceptable to the city, consistent with the city's Art in Public Places Implementing Guidelines.
The cost of the public art, as detennined pursuant to the Art in Public Places Implementing Guidelines,
shall be equal to at least two percent of the project's total construction cost.

  ATTACHMENT 1
   Ordinance No. 382
  Page 5 of6

  B.  In-lieu of placement of public art, the property owner may alternatively pay a public art
  contribution into the Public Art Fund, which shall be equal to at least one percent of the project's total
  construction cost.

  17.59.050  Procedures, Guidelines and Requirements.

  A.  The city council, by resolution, shall establish procedures, guidelines and requirements for the
  selection, approval, acquisition, placement, installation and maintenance of public art required by this
  chapter in the Art in Public Places hnplementing Guidelines.

  B.  Nothing contained in this chapter, or in any procedure promulgated hereunder, shall be construed
  so as to conflict with, or authorize any activity that is in violation of, any applicable local, state or federal
  law, rule, regulation or ordinance.

  17.59.060  Maintenance Requirements for Art Installations.

  Public art placed or installed pursuant to this chapter shall be permanently maintained by the property
  owner, unless the approval explicitly excludes maintenance, and shall not be removed, altered or relocated
  without obtaining prior written approval from the city pursuant to the Art in Public Places hnplementing
  Guidelines. A violation of this section is subject to the provisions of Chapters 1.08, 1.10 and 1.12.

  17.59.070  Public Art Fund.

  A.  In-lieu public art contributions collected pursuant to this chapter shall be paid to the city and
  deposited in the city's public art fund.

  B.  The city shall maintain a separate accounting of funds received pursuant to this chapter.

  C.  Funds collected pursuant to this chapter may only be used to acquire, place or install, and maintain
  public art throughout the city pursuant to the Art in Public Places hnplementing Guidelines.

  Section 5.  The City Clerk shall certify adoption of this ordinance.

  PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED this 22nd day of September 2014.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MALIBU
  APPROVING THE ART IN PUBLIC PLACES ORDINANCE IMPLEMENTING
  GUIDELINES, OUTLINING REVIEW PROCEDURES ASSOCIATED WITH
  PROJECTS THAT QUALIFY UNDER MALIBU MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION
  17.74.020

The City Council of the City of Malibu does hereby find, order and resolve as follows:

SECTION 1. Recitals.

  A.  On September 8, 2014, the City Council held a duly noticed public hearing on Zone
Text Amendment (ZTA) No. 13-009, introducing on first reading, Ordinance No. 3 82, as amended,
adding Chapter 17.59 (Art in Public Places) to Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal Code
(MMC) to create a public art requirement for certain commercial, institutional and multi-family
residential development projects.

  B.  On September 22, 2014, City Council held a second reading and approved adoption of
Ordinance No. 382 into the MMC.

  C.  On October 22, 2014, the Art in Public Places Ordinance (Ordinance), MMC Section
17.59 became effective and was added to the Malibu Municipal Code.

  D.  The City desires to adopt these Implementing Guidelines (Art Guidelines) to
implement MMC Chapter 17.59 (effective October 22, 2014) by establishing procedures and
guidelines for funding, selection, approval, acquisition, placement, installation, and maintenance of
artwork required by the MMC. These guidelines also apply to public art related to community-based
contributions and City-sponsored installations.

SECTION 2. Definitions.

  A.  "Art in Public Places Fund" (Public Art Fund) is a City agency account established
to maintain monies collected from the Ordinance or to accept contributions to fund placement of
public art.

  B.  "Conceptual Art Plan" (Art Plan) is a preliminary design of the proposed artwork,
proposed artist, proposed location, estimated total construction cost and preliminary art budget,
sufficient in scope and detail for the Cultural Arts Commission to review and provide
recommendations.

  C.  "Cultural Arts Selection Committee" (Selection Committee) means an independent
panel of arts industry professionals established for the purposes of providing the Cultural Arts
Commission with an artist/artwork recommendation.

  D.  "Final Art Plan" (Final Plan) is the final design of the artwork, final proposed
location, total construction cost for the qualifying project, and final art budget.

  E.  "Multi-Family Residential Development" means a building or portion thereof used
for occupancy by four or more families living independently of each other and containing four or
  ATTACHMENT2
   Resolution No. 17-35
  Page 2 of8

more dwelling units.

  F.  "Preliminary Art Budget" means a description of how the applicant proposes to
allocate the required 2% of total construction cost towards the proposed art as well as cost of the art
work, cost of transporting the art work, costs associated with installing the art work, including the
base, cost of and preliminary costs associated with placement.

  G.  "Remodel" means the upgrade of the interior or exterior faces of a building or
structure without altering the existing foundation, footprint or building envelope. "Remodeling" may
include the replacement of exterior walls within the limitations described herein and according to the
requirements of the building code, provided that such remodeling can meet the standards for zone
clearance or plot plan review.

SECTION 3. Public Art Requirement.

  The Ordinance requires property owners of certain commercial, industrial, and multi-family
developments to include an element of public art on the development site (or an approved alternative
site) or to make an in-lieu contribution to the Public Art Fund.

  Unless exempt pursuant to MMC Section 17.59.030(B), the applicant may select one of the
two options below to satisfy the Public Art Requirement:

  A.  Providing Public Art- The value of the art must be equal to at least two percent (2%)
of the project's Total Construction Cost.

  B.  In-Lieu Contribution - The in-lieu contribution must be equal to at least one percent
(1 %) of the project's Total Construction Cost.

SECTION 4. Implementation.

  A.  Install Public Art: The property owner shall acquire and install public aii consistent
with the Ordinance on the project site or an alternative site within and acceptable to the city. Project
must go through Review and Approval Process (see Exhibit A).

  B.  Pay In-Lieu Public Art Contribution (Art Contribution): In lieu of installation of
public art, the property owner may pay a public art contribution into the Public Art Fund as provided
in MMC Section l 7.59.040(B). The Art Contribution must be made prior to issuance of the building
permit.

SECTION 5. Initial Review and Approval Process.

  A.  Proposed Location for Art on Site Plan: Information regai·ding the Ordinance is
available to applicants from the Planning Department. All development projects that require the
inclusion of public art shall include the proposed location for the art on the site plan.

  ATTACHMENT 2
   Resolution No. 17-35
  Page 3 of8

  B.  Preliminary Art Budget Review: For projects requiring installation of public art
pursuant to the Ordinance, the property owner will prepare and submit to the City a Preliminary Art
Budget based on the estimated Total Construction Cost.

  C.  Conceptual Art Plan (Art Plan): Following City review and approval of the
Preliminary Art Budget, the property owner shall submit a Preliminary Art Plan for review by the
Selection Committee. Presentation materials should include slides, illustrations or photos of the artist's
work, sketches, drawings and a written text narrative of the conceptual art plari, including a statement of
qualifications for the artist supporting documentation and history of past projects.

The public art should relate to the overall development design. The property owner has the option of
presenting more than one Preliminary Art Plan for the same development project.

  D.  Art Review and Selection Process: The purpose for creating a review and selection
process is to provide a comprehensive, fair and transparent process in the selection and placement of
public art.

  Selection Committee: Each public art project may require the need to create
  an independent Selection Committee. Each Selection Committee member
  will possess the background, experience and qualifications in specific areas
  needed for the review of public art placement.

  The Selection Committee will be comprised oftwo Cultural Arts Commissioners,
  one art professional with knowledge in the applicable field, one artist with
  relevance to the needs of the project and one member of the community (with the
  appropriate knowledge needed for the project). Selection Committee members
  are tasked with reviewing artwork and providing recommendations to the
  Cultural Arts Commission based upon parameters established by the Cultural
  Arts Commission in reviewing each project.

  .2.  Selection Criteria: The Cultural Arts Commission will consider the following
  general criteria for the selection and placement of art considering that the art must
  comply with the requirements for structures in the zoning and noise ordinances:

  a. Media - all artwork mediums and materials will be considered.
  b. Style - Artwork reflecting any movement, method or style will be
  considered.
  c. Diversity- In selecting works, the Cultural Arts Commission will strive
  for diversity, reflecting the social, ethnic and cultural diversity.
  d. Relevance-Attwork that reflects the goals, objectives and culture of the
  City of Malibu.
  e. Artistic Excellence - Quality and assessment of the artist's concept and
  ability to execute the proposed work, based on previous artistic

  ATTACHMENT 2
   Resolution No. 17-35
  Page 4 of8

  achievement and experience or, in the case of an existing work of art, the
  quality of the executed work.
  f. Physical Durability- Consideration ofthe artwork's long-te1m durability
  against theft, vandalism, weather, structural and surface integrity, ease of
  maintenance as well as life span of piece on permanent installations.
  g. Public Safety-All proposals must adhere to public safety standards and
  all will be reviewed by the Community Services Director, Public Works
  Director, and City Manager.
  h. Costs- Consideration will be given to all costs of the project, including
  production, acquisition, sitting, installation, documentation and
  maintenance.
  1. Authenticity-Consideration will be given to the work in terms of value,
  legal title, and other issues as deemed appropriate.

3.  Art Media: The Cultural Arts Commission is receptive to the broadest definitions
  of art and encourages imaginative interpretations of all art media. The materials
  and media that may be used include, but are not limiti:;d to, the following:

  a. Original three-dimensional artworks;
  b. Original two-dimensional artworks; including but not limited to murals,
  photos, portable paintings;
  c. Environmental artwork;
  d. Any combination of media art;
  e. Fixtures, such as gates, streetlights, signage, public benches, paving,
  walkways, bus shelters, may be considered; and
  f. Facade treatments, hardscapes or functional elements that can be clearly
  differentiated from the original constrnction.
  g. The Public Alt Contribution should enhance the original construction,
  and should be documented and reflected in the construction budget as an
  enhancement.

  The following items are not considered artwork under these guidelines:

  h. Objects which are mass-produced from a standard design such as
  playground equipment, flags, banners or fountains;
  i. Reproductions, by mechanical or other means, of original artworks;
  J. Mass-produced directional elements or signage (except when an integral
  element of the original artwork) and super graphics; such as; large video
  screens, digital signs etc.
  k. Decorative, ornamental or functional elements which are designed by the
  building architect (i.e. not an element commissioned for the purpose of
  creating a unique work by an artist);
  I. Historic, architectural or art restoration/preservation efforts of building
  facades, architectural details, or existing artworks.

  ATTACHMENT 2
   Resolution No. 17-35
  Page 5 of8

  m. Lettering, logo, symbols and signage that is a commercial message; and
  n. Artwork containing obscene words, depictions, or representations.

  4.  Final Art Plan: The Final Art Plan (Final Plan) requires approval by the City
  Council prior to placement or installation of the artwork. The Final Art Plan
  shall consist of:

  a.  final art budget
  b.  final schematic design of the aitwork
  c.  final proposed location
  d.  final narrative with goals of project and description on plaque
  e.  maintenance plan
  f.  installation timeline
  g.  a two or three-dimensional sainple or rendering of the final piece

  If the total construction cost is different from the estimated total construction
  cost approved in the Art Plan, the art budget shall be adjusted accordingly to
  comply with the two percent (2%) requirement. The final art budget must also
  detail artist fees, and fabrication and installation expenses.

  Minor changes to the approved Final Plan or the conditions of approval, may be
  approved by the Community Services Department, provided that such changes
  substantially achieve the saine results and the project complies with the City
  Council's approval. Substantial changes, as determined by the Community
  Services Department, shall be re-submitted to the Cultural Arts Commission for
  review before City Council approval and prior to placement or installation ofthe
  artwork.

  5.  Final Approval: Prior to final inspection by the Environmental Sustainability
  Department or issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, staff from the Community
  Services Department shall inspect the project site to confirm the installation and
  placement ofthe artwork complies with the approved Final Plan. Final Building
  Safety Division approval shall not be issued until the Community Services
  Department has confirmed the project complies with the Final Plan or that the
  in-lieu contribution to the Public Art Fund has been received by the City.

SECTION 6. Value of Artwork.

  City staff will provide a detailed form requesting the costs associated with placement of public
art to applicants who intend to use art as part of their development. The value of the artwork must be
equal to at least two percent of the project's total construction cost. The Environmental Sustainability
Department will work with the applicant to determine such costs. The value of the artwork means the
cost of the public ait, as determined by the aforementioned review and approval procedures.

  ATTACHMENT2
   Resolution No. 17-35
  Page 6 of8

  A Selection Committee comprised of arts industry professionals will review the estimated value
of the artwork and costs associated with the placement and installation of the project. The value of the
artwork is determined by combining costs for acquisition, fabrication/construction, and installation.
Structural elements to secure or display the artwork, artist's professional fees and identification and
didactic information are also included in calculating the value of the artwork.

SECTION 7. Artwork Maintenance.

  The artwork approved and installed pursuant to the Ordinance is to be maintained by the
property owner throughout the life of the art. The property owner is responsible for any regular
maintenance and repairs in order to maintain the artwork to the condition it was at the time it
was originally installed. In the event the property owner wishes to remove, replace, or relocate the
artwork, the Community Services Department must be notified in writing 90 days prior to any
modification to the Final Plan. The replacement artwork will be subject to the same review process
as the original artwork, and the property owner will be required to submit an application pursuant to
the Ordinance. The Final Plan for the replacement artwork must be approved prior to the removal
of the previously approved artwork. Earlier removal of the existing artwork may be approved at the
discretion of the Community Services Department if the project poses a threat to public safety.

SECTION 8. Appeals.

  The applicant and any person adversely affected by the placement of art work required under
these Guidelines may appeal the decision within fifteen (I 5) days after the date of the decision to the
appropriate commission or board dependent on what component of the project is being appealed.
Any decision on an appeal by a commission or board may be appealed to the City Council.

SECTION 9. The City Council hereby accepts the Art in Public Places Ordinance Implementing
Guidelines and authorizes staff to begin implementing the Ordinance.

SECTION I 0. The City Clerk shall certify to the passage and adoption of this resolution and enter it
into the book of original resolutions.

PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED this 14th day of August 2017.
